Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accuses security officials of deliberately failing to wake him on the morning of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack, insisting the assault would have been contained had he intervened earlier - a day after his wife claimed an opposition figure knew of the attack in advance, prompting a threatened lawsuit. Netanyahu faces close-fought elections later in 2026. The 7 October attack killed more than 1,200 people in Israel and saw 251 taken hostage; Gaza authorities report more than 73,000 Palestinians killed in the offensive that followed.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli and Gaza authorities)

timeline.event: Unifil says the Israeli military has established four new bases in the areas of southern Lebanon it invaded, bringing the number of Israeli positions to nine, and reports consolidation and fortification of those positions along with demolition and engineering work. The strip under Israeli control is about 5 per cent of Lebanese territory and extends up to 10km from the border in places. A Lebanese intelligence official says Lebanon's military has recorded more than 5,000 violations of the June deal by Israel; the Israeli military says the buildings destroyed were used by Hezbollah for military purposes and that it acts in accordance with international law.
timeline.source: BBC (Unifil, Lebanese intelligence official, Israeli military)

timeline.event: More than 10 EU countries say they are willing to contribute to a planned European mission to train the Lebanese army.

Israel says a Hamas security chief was captured during a raid in Gaza City in which strikes killed four people, according to Gaza medics. Hezbollah's leader Naim Qassem last week called the US-brokered framework for the group's disarmament 'surrender with humiliation'.

Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry says Israeli attacks have killed more than 900 people in the territory so far in 2026 despite the ceasefire, taking the total since the 10 October truce past 1,300, including 301 children. The ministry does not separate civilians from combatants. The UN considers the figures reliable and BBC Verify says independent analysis is consistent with them; the Israeli military disputes the count, saying there is no basis to assume all those listed were killed by its activity, and says five of its soldiers have been killed in combat since the ceasefire.

A BBC team travelling with Unifil inside the part of southern Lebanon under Israeli control reports entire villages flattened, with air strikes and demolitions continuing after the ceasefire announced in June. Lebanese officials say Israel is expanding its positions in the zone.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: DR Congo's own health data now puts its Ebola death toll above 3,000, with 6,186 confirmed cases — a national count running well ahead of WHO's last ratified figures and confirming the epidemic is still accelerating rather than levelling off. It is already the largest outbreak in Congo's history and second only to West Africa's in 2014-16, and with Uganda's and France's monitoring windows now closed it is a single-country emergency being fought with a vaccine nobody yet knows works against this strain. Everything else on the board is seasonal rather than alarming: cholera concentrated overwhelmingly in Nigeria, West Nile still creeping north through Europe. The one to act on locally is Singapore's flu wave — if you are older or have a chronic condition, this is the week for the jab.

outbreaks.name: DR Congo — Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: Still a Public Health Emergency of International Concern; new confirmed cases now only in DR Congo
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO-confirmed cumulative figures as of 26 August, re-read this run from Disease Outbreak News 616 (published 28 August and still WHO's newest — the DON API shows nothing after it): 5,794 cases in DR Congo (including two patients diagnosed there and later treated in Germany), 20 in Uganda and one in France. The 2,788 deaths include two in Uganda; at least 1,314 patients have recovered. DR Congo's own health data, reported on 2 September, is now well ahead of that: 6,186 confirmed cases and 3,007 deaths, a national count WHO has not yet ratified in a DON (Al Jazeera reported the same government series at 6,100 cases and 2,950 deaths on 31 August). ECDC's week-35 threats report cites DRC's count of 5,794 confirmed cases and 2,786 deaths as of 27 August. The 42-day monitoring period closed in both Uganda and France on 27 August, and WHO began Ervebo vaccination of health workers in DRC on 27 August, though the vaccine's protection against Bundibugyo virus in humans is unknown. An IHR Emergency Committee met on 18 August and the Director-General kept the PHEIC in place. This is the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in DRC, of any species, and second only to the 2014-16 West African epidemic.

outbreaks.name: Global — cholera
outbreaks.status: Still spreading across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas; Nigeria dominates the current wave
outbreaks.scope_note: Worldwide totals since 1 January 2026, re-read this run directly from ECDC's week-35 Communicable Disease Threats Report PDF (28 August, still the newest issued). Between 27 July and 26 August, 42,717 new cases and 257 new deaths were reported; Nigeria alone accounted for 41,296 cases and 242 deaths, followed by Angola (524), Somalia (489), Mozambique (319) and Chad (47). The country count is the 19 countries that reported new cases in that month. For comparison, the same period of 2025 had recorded 338,340 cases and 4,324 deaths. ECDC warns that case definitions, testing strategies and reporting completeness vary widely between countries, so the totals are an undercount.

outbreaks.name: United States — measles
outbreaks.status: Worst US year since elimination was declared in 2000; count still climbing
outbreaks.scope_note: CDC's confirmed 2026 count as of its 27 August data date, still the latest published figure this run: 2,887 cases reported by 47 jurisdictions plus 16 among international visitors, across 37 outbreaks, with 94% of confirmed cases (2,737 of 2,903) outbreak-associated. CDC's own measles data page returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool again this run, so the figure was read from that page's content via search and corroborated against independent reporting of the same CDC update. About 92% of cases were in people who were unvaccinated or of unknown vaccination status. CDC's national total records no measles deaths; Pennsylvania has separately reported two deaths in unvaccinated residents that CDC does not include.

outbreaks.name: Europe — West Nile virus
outbreaks.status: Seasonal transmission still expanding; 25 newly affected areas in a single week
outbreaks.scope_note: Locally acquired human cases in the 2026 season as at 26 August, re-read this run from ECDC's weekly WNV dashboard (week 35, produced 27 August at 12:45 and still the latest — week 36 has not been issued): Italy 428, Greece 222 (eight with unknown place of infection), Spain 79, North Macedonia 49, Romania 45, France 28, Serbia 11, Croatia 3, the Netherlands 3, and one or two each in Austria, Cyprus, Germany, Albania, Hungary and Kosovo. The same report counts 124 affected areas across those 15 countries, 25 of them reported affected for the first time this season. ECDC does not publish a season-wide death count for WNV, hence the dash.

stories.headline: DR Congo's own data puts its Ebola death toll above 3,000
stories.summary: Congolese government figures released on Sep 2 show 3,007 deaths and 6,186 confirmed cases, making this the largest and deadliest Ebola epidemic in the country's history and second only to the 2014-16 West African outbreak. The national series is ahead of WHO's last ratified count of 5,815 confirmed cases and 2,788 deaths as of 26 August; Al Jazeera reported the same government data at 6,100 cases and 2,950 deaths on 31 August, so the trajectory is corroborated. The outbreak was declared in Ituri province on 15 May and has since reached six provinces. WHO estimates 60 per cent of deaths occurred outside treatment centres. Bundibugyo virus has no approved vaccine; DRC has begun giving frontline health workers Merck's Ervebo, licensed against the Zaire species and believed to offer some cross-protection.
stories.source: The Straits Times, Al Jazeera (DRC health ministry)

stories.headline: UK pledges a further £50 million to contain DR Congo's Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Britain said it would provide more than £50 million (about US$67.6 million) in new funding for the response in DR Congo, where confirmed cases have passed 6,000 in the country's largest-ever epidemic. That national figure runs ahead of WHO's last formally ratified count of 5,815 confirmed cases as of 26 August.

stories.headline: Influenza climbs in Singapore, with more than a third of community swabs testing positive
stories.summary: The Communicable Diseases Agency reported a rise in influenza activity and urged people at higher risk of severe illness to get vaccinated, while saying there is no indication current infections are more severe than usual.
stories.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Communicable Diseases Agency)

stories.headline: WHO keeps DR Congo Ebola emergency in place as confirmed cases reach 5,815
stories.summary: Disease Outbreak News 616 records 5,815 confirmed Bundibugyo virus cases and 2,788 deaths as of 26 August, with new confirmed cases since the 14 August report reported only in DR Congo. Following the second IHR Emergency Committee meeting on 18 August, the Director-General kept the outbreak classified as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern and issued updated temporary recommendations. Vaccination of health workers with Ervebo began in some areas including Kisangani on 27 August, alongside a clinical trial, since it is not known whether the vaccine protects against Bundibugyo virus in humans.

stories.headline: ECDC declares Uganda's Ebola outbreak closed while DRC transmission continues
stories.summary: The 42-day enhanced monitoring period required by international guidance was completed in both Uganda and France on 27 August, leaving DR Congo as the only country still reporting new confirmed cases. WHO says the intensity of transmission there means the risk of further cross-border exportation remains.
stories.source: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report, week 35; WHO DON616

stories.headline: Global cholera adds 42,717 cases in a month, four in five of them in Nigeria
stories.summary: ECDC's week-35 report records 42,717 new cases and 257 new deaths worldwide between 27 July and 26 August, across 19 countries. Nigeria accounted for 41,296 of those cases and 242 of the deaths. The 2026 running total of 212,857 cases and 1,943 deaths is well below the 338,340 cases and 4,324 deaths recorded over the same period of 2025.
stories.source: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report, week 35

stories.headline: Fatal diphtheria case in an unvaccinated four-year-old in Sicily
stories.summary: ECDC's week-35 threats report notes a fatal diphtheria case in an unvaccinated four-year-old child in Sicily, Italy.
stories.source: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report, week 35

stories.headline: Second human swine-flu A(H1N2)v case linked to a Michigan county fair
stories.summary: ECDC's week-35 report, citing US CDC, records a second human infection with swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v associated with a county fair in Michigan. Cases of this kind follow direct contact with pigs and there is no evidence of sustained human-to-human spread.
stories.source: ECDC Communicable Disease Threats Report, week 35 (US CDC)

stories.headline: West Nile virus reaches 877 human cases across 15 European countries
stories.summary: ECDC's week-35 dashboard counts 877 locally acquired human cases this season across 15 countries and 124 affected areas, 25 of which were reported affected for the first time this season. Italy leads with 428 cases, followed by Greece with 222 and Spain with 79.
stories.source: ECDC weekly West Nile virus surveillance report, week 35

stories.headline: EU studying a European version of Singapore's Project Wolbachia for dengue
stories.summary: Mosquito populations at Singapore's Project Wolbachia sites have fallen 80 to 90 per cent, and the European Union is assessing whether a comparable release programme would work in Europe.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Three internet-facing products are under active exploitation, and SonicWall's SMA1000 VPN appliances are the one to handle first: two zero-days the vendor says are being chained in live attacks. Behind them sit Sangoma Switchvox, where a CVSS 9.3 SQL injection has been handing unauthenticated attackers reverse shells since 30 August, and a JFrog Artifactory authentication weakness being used to mint admin tokens. Then PaperCut — CISA added both of its zero-days to the exploited catalogue on 31 August and they are now driving data theft. On the breach side the numbers are large: roughly 5,000 Dropbox accounts taken through a legacy Lenovo ID link, and 9.5 million patients exposed at Aesto Health. The AI-adjacent items read as trend rather than emergency, including a stolen key that burned US$600,000 in credits — and if your alert queue filled with Safe Links detections today, that is a Microsoft misclassification, not an attack.

stories.headline: Dropbox accounts breached through a Lenovo ID email-verification flaw
stories.summary: Dropbox says about 5,000 accounts were accessed between Aug 4 and Aug 21 after an attacker exploited a weakness in Lenovo's email verification to register Lenovo IDs using victims' email addresses, then used those IDs to sign in through a legacy Lenovo-Dropbox identity link. Content was viewed and downloaded from some accounts. Lenovo says its own customers were not affected. Dropbox has expired all sessions authenticated via Lenovo ID and now requires a Dropbox password alongside Lenovo ID sign-in. If you ever linked a Lenovo ID, check your Dropbox sign-in history.

stories.headline: Microsoft Defender is flagging legitimate Google search links as malicious
stories.summary: Microsoft acknowledged an incident, tracked as MO1465962, in which Defender for Office 365 Safe Links misclassifies legitimate Google search URLs as malicious. Administrators are seeing spurious alerts and incidents in both the Defender portal and Sentinel, and pasting a blocked link straight into a browser does not bypass the warning because the classification itself is wrong. Microsoft says it is correcting the misclassification and has filed it as an advisory.

stories.headline: GeoNetwork patches an unauthenticated RCE chain sitting behind government geoportals
stories.summary: Two flaws in the GeoNetwork geospatial metadata catalogue can be chained for unauthenticated remote code execution: a missing authorisation check on the formatter upload endpoint (CVE-2026-63219, CVSS 8.6) plus code execution through an unsafe Saxon XSLT configuration in the formatter (CVE-2026-58400). Fixes shipped in 4.4.12 and 4.2.17 on Jul 8 and details were published on Aug 31. Researchers found 121 exposed GeoNetwork 4.x deployments across 39 countries, 89 per cent of them government, military or national-agency systems. If you cannot patch immediately, block POST, PUT and PATCH to /geonetwork/srv/api/formatters at the reverse proxy.

stories.headline: Sality botnet infrastructure dismantled in a joint international takedown
stories.summary: The US Justice Department, FBI and DCIS, working with Europol, Eurojust and authorities in Bulgaria, Hungary and Romania plus CrowdStrike, seized Sality-linked domains in the US and Europe and ran a peer-to-peer sinkhole operation that isolated infected machines and purged their peer lists. Over 15,000 devices have been infected since the malware first appeared in 2003. The two still-active Sality networks were mainly delivering EggJagger, a clipboard hijacker that swaps cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the operator's own. CrowdStrike tracks the group as SALTY SPIDER.

stories.headline: Russian national extradited over an Excel macro campaign that hit 80,000 freelancers
stories.summary: US prosecutors charged Searzhudin Tamirlanovich Aktulaev, 40, over a campaign that infected roughly 80,000 freelancers — about half of them in the US — with the TVRAT and DarkVNC remote-access tools between June 2016 and November 2017. He is accused of using 255 fake accounts to send malicious Excel attachments through a freelance platform's messaging system, stealing e-commerce credentials and personal data. He was arrested at Larnaca Airport in Cyprus in May 2025 and extradited; the 2021 indictment was unsealed this week.

stories.headline: Researchers used Claude to port a pre-auth PLC exploit to a different controller
stories.summary: Forescout's Vedere Labs used Anthropic's Claude to move a working pre-authentication RCE exploit for CVE-2021-31886 — a Nucleus FTP server buffer overflow — from a WAGO 750-852 PLC to a 750-831, executing ARM shellcode on live hardware. The point is the cost curve, not a new flaw: it took heavy researcher supervision, hand-fed disassembly context and about US$536 in API spend over 8.5 hours for the final stage, though once code execution worked the model produced two functional payloads in 12 minutes. Read it as evidence that exploit porting for legacy OT is getting cheaper, and patch or segment old PLCs accordingly.

stories.headline: Critical Switchvox SQL injection exploited to drop reverse shells without credentials
stories.summary: Horizon3.ai says exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-9586 in Sangoma Switchvox SMB Edition began on Aug 30. The /pa endpoint concatenates a user-controlled PhoneIP value from XML into PostgreSQL queries without parameterisation, letting an unauthenticated attacker run code as the PostgreSQL superuser, read and modify the database and escalate to Switchvox web administrator. NVD rates it 9.3. Sangoma patched it in Switchvox 8.4.0.2 on Jul 14; roughly 4,000 instances remain exposed to the internet, most in the US.

stories.headline: SonicWall says two SMA1000 zero-days are being chained in live attacks
stories.summary: SonicWall warned that two previously unknown flaws in its SMA 1000 remote-access appliances are under active exploitation and may form an attack chain. NVD currently carries a 7.8 base score for CVE-2026-83549 and has not yet scored CVE-2026-83548; neither has been added to CISA's known-exploited catalogue at the time of writing, so the exploited status rests on SonicWall's own advisory and the reporting around it. SMA 1000 is an internet-facing VPN gateway, so treat this as patch-now.

stories.headline: Phishing crews abuse the Faronics Deploy admin tool to install ScreenConnect
stories.summary: Attackers are using Faronics Deploy, a legitimate endpoint management product, to push ScreenConnect onto victim machines, giving them remote control without dropping obviously malicious tooling. Because both products are signed and commonly used by IT teams, the activity blends into normal administration; hunt for unexpected Faronics and ScreenConnect installs rather than relying on signature detection.

stories.headline: Aesto Health breach exposes data on more than 9.5 million patients
stories.summary: The healthcare technology firm says a breach affects over 9.5 million patients. It is one of the larger US healthcare disclosures this year; the company has not detailed the intrusion route.

stories.headline: Critical Langflow RCE exploited to steal OpenAI and AWS keys
stories.summary: Attackers are exploiting a code-injection flaw in the Langflow AI workflow builder, rated 9.8 by NVD, to run code on exposed servers and harvest the OpenAI and AWS credentials stored in them. Reporting also ties the same activity cluster to probing of a critical Ruby on Rails flaw for credential theft and command-and-control. Anyone running Langflow on an internet-reachable host should patch and rotate every key the instance held.

stories.headline: Attackers mint Artifactory admin tokens days after the JFrog patch shipped
stories.summary: An authentication weakness in JFrog Artifactory, rated 9.8 by NVD, lets attackers create administrator access tokens under default configuration, and exploitation began within days of disclosure. Artifactory usually holds an organisation's build artefacts and internal packages, so a compromise is a direct route into the software supply chain. Note this is a separate issue from CVE-2026-66384, the medium-severity Artifactory path flaw CISA added to its exploited catalogue on Aug 27.

stories.headline: Breeze Comet ran hundreds of fraudulent transfers through Brazilian payment rails
stories.summary: A financially motivated group tracked as Breeze Comet executed hundreds of fraudulent transactions through Brazilian payment systems. The pattern matches a run of attacks on Latin American payment infrastructure in which intruders reach the institution's payment integration layer rather than individual customer accounts.

stories.headline: BGP hijack used to push a malicious Virtualizor update to hosting providers
stories.summary: Attackers hijacked BGP routes to impersonate the update infrastructure for Virtualizor, a VPS control panel, and served a malicious update to hosting providers. Routing-layer interception defeats the usual trust in an update endpoint's hostname, so operators should verify package signatures and check for unexpected Virtualizor updates in the affected window.

stories.headline: Novocure breach affects more than 1,400 cancer patients
stories.summary: The oncology device maker disclosed a breach involving the data of over 1,400 cancer patients. The company has not published details of how the intrusion occurred.

stories.headline: 13 malicious Packagist packages target unpatched iPhones to steal wallet seeds
stories.summary: Thirteen packages published to the PHP package registry Packagist served an exploit chain at visitors on out-of-date iPhones, aiming to extract cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases. Keeping iOS current blocks the chain; developers should also audit recent Packagist pulls.

stories.headline: Iranian group poses as recruiters, using fake coding tests to drop cross-platform RATs
stories.summary: An Iran-linked crew is approaching targets as recruiters and delivering remote-access trojans inside take-home coding assignments, with builds for multiple operating systems. The lure works because running unfamiliar code is the expected behaviour in the scenario — treat any recruiter-supplied project as untrusted and run it only in a disposable VM.

stories.headline: Nearly 22,000 Exchange servers still unpatched against a mailbox-takeover flaw
stories.summary: Scans found close to 22,000 internet-facing Microsoft Exchange servers still vulnerable to a capture-replay authentication bypass that NVD rates 8.0 and that can lead to mailbox hijacking. The fix has been available for weeks; unpatched on-premises Exchange remains one of the most reliable footholds attackers have.

stories.headline: Stolen METR API key burned about US$600,000 of AI credits
stories.summary: Attackers who obtained an API key belonging to research organisation METR consumed roughly US$600,000 in AI credits over about three weeks before it was caught. It is a clean illustration of why model-provider keys need spend caps, per-key alerting and rotation on the same footing as cloud credentials.

stories.headline: UAC-0099 plants a 'nuclear weapon' prompt in malware to derail AI code analysis
stories.summary: The Russia-aligned group UAC-0099 embedded text in its malware designed to trip the safety filters of AI assistants used by analysts, so that automated triage refuses to examine the sample. It is an early example of prompt injection aimed at the defender's tooling rather than the victim's.

stories.headline: PaperCut zero-days now used for data theft, and both are in CISA's exploited catalogue
stories.summary: Two recently patched PaperCut NG/MF flaws are being used in data-theft attacks. CISA added both to its known-exploited catalogue on Aug 31: CVE-2026-82078, an unsafe dynamic class-loading issue in the database connection utilities that NVD rates 9.4, and CVE-2026-81578, an improper access control flaw in the web management interface rated 8.8. Print servers are often forgotten in patch cycles and sit deep inside the network — check yours.

stories.headline: Cronos blockchain restarted after a US$74 million Tectonic exploit
stories.summary: The Cronos chain was halted and then restarted following an exploit of the Tectonic lending protocol that drained about US$74 million. Halting a chain to contain a protocol-level loss remains contentious among users who expect it to keep running regardless.

stories.headline: TerminalFix uses fake Cloudflare CAPTCHAs to open reverse tunnels into networks
stories.summary: A campaign tracked as TerminalFix serves counterfeit Cloudflare CAPTCHA pages that talk users through pasting a command into a terminal, which installs a reverse-tunnel backdoor into the internal network. The 'paste this to verify you're human' pattern is now common enough that it belongs in user awareness training.

stories.headline: North Korean fake-worker fraud spreads from IT roles into healthcare and sales
stories.summary: North Korean operatives placing fraudulent remote workers inside Western companies have moved beyond software engineering into healthcare and sales positions. That widens the exposure beyond the engineering hiring pipeline, so identity verification at onboarding needs to cover every remote role, not just technical ones.

stories.headline: China-linked Fire Ant turns Cisco IOS XR routers into covert spying platforms
stories.summary: The group tracked as Fire Ant is hijacking Cisco routers to harvest credentials in transit and suppress security logging, leaving little evidence on the device. Network gear that sits below the reach of EDR is an increasingly favoured foothold; verify router images and export logs off-box.

stories.headline: Aurora ransomware operators used the Cursor AI coding agent during intrusions
stories.summary: Operators behind the Aurora ransomware used the Cursor AI coding assistant for hands-on-keyboard work against about 10 targets, according to researchers. It is another data point in AI tooling being folded into ordinary intrusion tradecraft rather than enabling anything qualitatively new.
